analysis.summary: The PR introduces logic errors in the pricing display, specifically regarding falsy numeric checks and incorrect fallback behavior between VAT-inclusive and VAT-exclusive values.

bugs.title: Falsy fallback for zero-value discount percentage
bugs.description: The use of the logical OR operator (||) for totalDiscountPercentage will cause the UI to incorrectly fall back to the VAT-inclusive discount percentage if the net discount is exactly 0. In JavaScript, 0 is falsy, so the expression will evaluate the right side of the operator even if the net discount is explicitly 0%.
bugs.risk: Displays incorrect financial data to the user. A product with no net discount (0%) will incorrectly show the gross discount percentage (e.g., 5%) when showVat is false.

bugs.title: Incorrect cross-contamination of VAT and Net discount data
bugs.description: When showVat is false, the component is intended to show net (VAT-exclusive) values. However, for both discountPercentage and discountAmount, the logic falls back to the VAT-inclusive 'discount' field if the 'netDiscount' field is missing or falsy. This is inconsistent with the 'cashPrice' logic in the same block, which correctly defaults to '-' if the net price is missing.
bugs.risk: Creates a UI data mismatch where a user might see a net cash price (without VAT) paired with a gross discount amount (including VAT), or see a discount for a price that is marked as unavailable.

notBugs.reason: The change of discountAmount from number to string is applied consistently across the Price and CashBuyPrice components, and the value passed (formattedValue) matches this new type.
The rename appears to be a typo fix or a standard refactor that has been applied to both the TypeScript interface and the consumption logic in the pricing component.
